articles.title: Meet China’s giant Jiutian drone: 6-tonne payload, 12-hour endurance and a swarm-carrying design; how powerful is Beijing’s flying mothership?
articles.description: China has flown its large, jet-powered Jiutian drone for the first time. The aircraft is much bigger than many military drones in service today. Its size also gives it room to carry a heavy payload, including equipment designed to release swarms of smaller drones. Built by AVIC, the jet-powered aircraft can carry up to six tonnes and stay airborne for 12 hours. The drone can reportedly reach speeds of up to 378 knots and operate at altitudes of up to 15,000 metres.

articles.title: BT EXCLUSIVE| Should India Fear Starlink's Satellite Dominance? OneWeb's Neha Idnani Responds
articles.description: Starlink's entry into India, satellite spectrum, licensing approvals and the future of satellite internet have become some of the most debated topics in the telecom sector. In an exclusive conversation with Business Today at India Mobile Congress 2026, Eutelsat OneWeb Asia-Pacific Head Neha Idnani discusses India's satellite communications framework, explains why satellite should complement rather than replace telecom networks, details how OneWeb uses satellite connectivity during disasters, and responds to concerns over Starlink's rapidly expanding satellite constellation. She also explains why India should not be worried about growing competition in satellite communications and why multiple operators can coexist in the market. Business Today's Aishwarya Patil speaks with Neha Idnani. Listen In to this Exclusive conversation.

articles.title: Russia Sending Iranian Diesel To US After Deal With Trump? Bombshell Claim
articles.description: Is Russia reselling Iranian diesel to the United States? Unverified claims suggest that some of the fuel Moscow has promised to supply to Washington could have originated in Iran, raising questions about the real source of Russia’s diesel exports. US President Donald Trump has announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release hundreds of thousands of metric tons of diesel into American and global markets in an effort to ease soaring fuel costs ahead of the November midterm elections. But Russia’s ability to meet those commitments faces a major challenge as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to hit Russian oil refineries.
